chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Abu Al-Maghra', from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) permitted the women and children to depart at night, to pelt the Jamarat at night, and to pray the morning prayer in their homes. So if they feared menstruation, they would go to Mecca, and they would appoint someone to offer the sacrifice on their behalf.
ai.seo_question: What are the Hajj concessions for women and children regarding departure time, stoning, and sacrifice?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the practical flexibility (rukhas) granted to women and children during Hajj, specifically permitting them to depart Muzdalifa before dawn and perform stoning and Fajr prayer at home to avoid the crowds and heat. It further addresses the specific concern of menstruation by allowing a proxy to offer the sacrifice, reflecting the Shia emphasis on ease in religious obligations. This ruling is often discussed in fiqh manuals regarding the validity of night-time stoning and the specific exemptions for those with valid excuses.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Abu Al magra, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allahsaww permitted for the women and the children that they can depart at night, and pelt the Jamarah at night; and that they should Pray the morning (Prayer) in their houses. So if they fear the menstruation, they should go to Makkah, and every one of them should offer a sacrifice of their behalf’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from abu al-Mughirah from abu Basir who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, permitted women and children to leave during the night to throw pebbles on Jamarat during the night and perform the morning Salat (prayer) in their lodgings. If women are afraid of Hayd (menses), the should proceed to Makkah and appoint someone to slaughter the offering on their behalf.”
